# Summary
His name is Alfred Pennyworth, and he has been away from Gotham for far too long. He’s been pulled away from a target that he has been tracking for the past 5 years in order to observe a group in Gotham called The Party Animals. This violent group has been terrorizing and killing the people of Gotham with no mercy, even burning down schools, police stations, all without any revealed motivation. Alfred has been assigned to observe, but not engage, for there is another player in town that is a mystery to his higher ups. 

![image](https://image.nostr.build/bb1e589aeab7c6b0dbc015656fea86ea04d0ee99bf2371fe74d68100b2418446.jpg)

The tension in the city is thick with fear as Mayor Jim Gordan calls for a town meeting. The public cry for his resignation, calling him and the police of this city cowards. While some people in the crowd stand to inspire the city to fight back against this terrorist group, the doors are kicked down and gunfire sprays across the platform. Panic ensues as the Gotham Police Department begins to  secure the scene, but climbing the stairs of the capitol building is a horde of Party Animal Members, wielding any weapon they can get their hands on. 

![image](https://image.nostr.build/0eb5d6a6aac713bcf808970213ac175335459ff6b01298af267df0ee655c1459.jpg)

Dread is setting in for the few police officers holding the line. Just as there about to make their move, an upside down masked vigilante pushes them back into their secure room and tells them “Whatever you hear, you do not open this door”. Batman goes to work, disarming the attackers, employing some incredible fighting techniques, and showing off plenty of tech that shows us what kind of a fighter he truly is. Alfred observes from his vantage point, ignoring his order from the higher up to engage Batman, and moves in to try and apprehend him. Batman outmaneuvers him quite spectacularly. 

![image](https://image.nostr.build/2d0117ba456530ecdf65d4822a508b08356a0d5e8ab28023e06c47f8e9f8ae6d.jpg)

Between Alfred’s connections and Bruce Wayne’s flashbacks we start to see what led to the Batman’s debut. It all began at shooting at the zoo where his father was killed. While Bruce led a life of rebellion in his early days, he refocused his efforts and ended up at the best university in the state. He studied mechanics, chemistry, criminal psychology, military theory, and sociocultural history. He then came home, back to Gotham, where he took on any job that connected him to the city. From the water department, all the way up to an engineer, all for the purpose of understanding the heartbeat of Gotham.

In the end Alfred makes an attempt to apprehend him but, just as last time, fails. Batman steals his motorcycle and rides off into the night as he tries to stem the bleeding of a corrupted city. 

![image](https://image.nostr.build/ed90ada4403c235be97c8f75f5d3f1cf7adbe2d7d3d689c935864321dfe97957.jpg)

# Review
All right everyone, I know I am incredibly late when it comes to jumping into the Absolute Universe but I am really excited to finally talk about it. What an jaw dropping way to set the tone for Batman going forward. This issue really makes the city of Gotham feel alive and grounds it into reality. We can feel the heartbeat of the city and the chaos that is pumping through the streets as we start to internalize what the Party Animals are doing. There is grit when it comes to this comic. It’s dark, grounded, but still stretches your mind when it comes to what Batman is capable of doing. We see that his upbringing isn’t simply going to far off lands and learning different styles of combat. This version of Batman wants to understand the city, what makes it tick, and what can be done to keep his patient alive.

![image](https://image.nostr.build/86546bfce1e808111f79f4739681f8721865a0d35050d01fc701465a5cd89f6e.jpg)

The little twists we see from what we are used to in Batman stories don’t feel wacky or cheap. They feel purposeful and give this story something for us to chew on. Seeing Alfred as a highly trained assassin puts us on edge since it is such a departure from what we are used to. He isn’t someone who is serving Batman to fulfil his purpose, he is now a foil that Batman needs to overcome. The classic villains we all know and love are not just tragic villains, but are Bruce’s childhood friends that gives him a stake in these characters futures. It all is culminating into a story that gives us the comfort of reading something familiar, but enough differences that is going to make this story exciting to read every month. 

![image](https://image.nostr.build/fafb665739d1f5a52d28de944933ff3bd0b19571a4b51385d852942951270664.jpg)

One sign for me of a superhero comic book having legs is if they can keep my attention during multiple page fights scenes and this one definitely did it. While it’s really cool to see Batman use gadgets that we have never seen before, it also does a great job of using restrained overexaggeration that gives some weight to each action.  I was truly gripped by each panel, even the smaller ones that hyper focus on a single moment within the entire fight sequence. 

I think we have an incredible story on our hands that is going to redefine who Batman is and I am always excited to look through a different lens when it comes to a character that is universally known. 

# The Moments

![image](https://image.nostr.build/bc8a4068bb9ec149f9aca9efb3b5a6868100a1c2beb9b16688f3195b88a74031.jpg)
![image](https://image.nostr.build/9c87e44bf2983977862336ae3cd9f2822d06c4af176680d33c81831c9f7efd3b.jpg)
This issue does a great job when it comes to showing us contrast. We get to see the kids at the zoo, happy as can be, anbd then we see the title page - the image of a handgun, already putting us on edge in terms of Bruce’s back story. Croc’s Gym stands alone amongst a pile of rubble while new construction is beginning, showing us that he wont give into the big guys upstairs. As Alfred is driving into town we get the image of a homeless camp on one side and a luxury car dealership on the other. It’s a really quiet way for the story to steer our emotions and to flesh out a location effectively. 

![image](https://image.nostr.build/8e56d8fcb14c81ff6caa055192d92178e00766989145fd4e9198b78260fbbae3.jpg)![image](https://image.nostr.build/366310f6fcc4722e78c3a94b43094626869b6401b2bbd503d3df65f0359cb41e.jpg)
Batman has always used the symbol of the bat to strike fear into his enemies, but at times it feels like that’s as far as it goes. I like the fact that he’s taking the lifestyle of bats and turning them into weapons that not only are effective, but adds to this terrifying persona that Batman uses to his advantage. 

![image](https://image.nostr.build/44d5a86fae645dbad0dbc30e66d5ae17d6b933ef9be85434ce277dd99db2af64.jpg)
Do I need to even say anything? A true jaw dropping moment for me when I read it and I remember this image making the rounds on social media. I think it just fortifies what I said above, he’s taking this symbol of the bat and weaponizing it, and in this case in a literal way. I think it’s really an incredibly multipurpose device that can protect his vital organs in a fire fight, be used as a melee weapon when it calls for it, and it just helps him train even in action with the weight of it right on his chest.

![image](https://image.nostr.build/72db4665ff150c7108fa422bcd5687e4b616857ea471f36355d10e70bc56694e.jpg)

This is going to a really fun series to cover and I’m shooting to branch into the other Absolute Books, which is going to be an adventure because I don’t really have anything to compare them to. While I know who The Flash, Green Lantern, and the Green Arrow are, I have never cracked open another one of their others books set in the ‘Main Line’ universe. Keep your eyes on the website and I’ll get these reviews out when I can.
